Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn these field notes into an accessibility audit briefing for the north quay interchange, and address the draft to Leonie, not Ellis. this is a fictional site visit on 14 may by the city access review team, with mara chen taking notes and tomas reed checking the route. cover the interchange and the adjoining quay street bus stops, but don't make claims about the whole transit network. the point is to give the facilities group a usable account of what was observed and what still needs checking; don't write a pass/fail verdict. keep the difference clear between an observation, a staff explanation, and a question we haven't resolved.

we started at the east entrance at 8:20 in light rain. the automatic doors opened on the first approach during three trials, but the clear opening looked narrower when a person stood beside the door; no tape measurement was taken, and the note says the fixed sign may be reducing the usable width. the tactile paving runs from the entrance toward the lift lobby, though one paving strip ends about a metre short of the lobby threshold and there is a smooth tile gap. a delivery trolley was parked partly over the strip at 8:34, then gone when we came back at 9:05. do not say it was there all morning. the desk clerk said deliveries are usually moved before the peak, but we didn't ask who is responsible for moving them. there is a bench near the entrance, with an armrest only at one end; we saw no reserved seating sign.

at the lift lobby the north lift was in service, and the south lift displayed an out-of-service notice. the notice gave no return time. mara noted that the nearest stairs are around the corner, not directly opposite the lobby. the call button on the north lift responded, but the panel's lower button row was partly hidden by a temporary event poster taped to the wall, not over the buttons. the lift was observed arriving after roughly 40 seconds once, not timed on repeated trips. inside, the floor indicator worked and the spoken floor announcement was audible from the doorway, but no one assessed its volume from the back of a crowded car. a staff member said the south lift had stopped that morning and a contractor had been contacted; there was no work order available to the review team. include that as an attributed explanation, not a confirmed repair schedule.

we followed the signed accessible route to platform 2. a blue wayfinding arrow at the corridor junction pointed toward platform 2 and the bus connection, but the smaller print below it was hard to read from the approach. the next sign was mounted behind a temporary queue barrier. at the platform entrance, the tactile warning surface was present, but the edge of one tile looked raised. we did not test it or estimate the height. the platform and train interface varied by vehicle: on the train that arrived at 8:52, the gap looked wider near the second carriage than near the first, and the train stopped with its first doorway just beyond the painted boarding marker. this was a visual observation from one arrival, not a measured gap or a statement about every train. no ramp was requested or deployed during the visit. a passenger asked the station host, “is the lift at the far end working today?” and the host pointed back toward the lobby; we couldn't hear the rest of their exchange.

at quay street, the two bus stops are on opposite sides of the access road. the stop serving routes 6 and 18 has a shelter and a timetable case; the case was fogged inside, so the printed times could not be read during the visit. the stop for route 41 has a pole and no shelter. the kerb at the route 6/18 stop was not measured. a parked maintenance van partly blocked the landing area at 9:18, with a gap still open behind it; the driver wasn't present, and we don't know how long it stayed. the route 41 pole had a route label facing the road, while the small stop name plate faced the pavement. the bus driver on route 6 lowered the vehicle ramp after a wheelchair user waited at the stop. note only that one observed boarding; we didn't speak with the passenger or ask whether the ramp met their needs.

mara checked the public information displays and the help point. the departures screen at the main hall showed platform information for the next two trains; the review team did not compare it with the live control system. the wall-mounted help point lit when pressed, and a voice answered after about 25 seconds. we did not test the hearing loop or confirm whether the call was logged. the staff member answering asked which entrance the caller was near, but our note does not record the caller's answer. do not infer that the help point is accessible in every respect from the light and voice response. the printed large-text map was available at the information desk, but the clerk said copies had run low; there were two visible when we checked at 9:40. no one asked for a copy during the visit.

organize the requested briefing so the reader can distinguish the route from the observations at each point. use a short opening that gives the date, team, and scope, then a numbered section for the main locations: 1) east entrance and lift lobby, 2) platform 2, 3) quay street bus stops, and 4) information and help point. within each location, separate what we directly saw from what staff told us and what remains unknown where that distinction applies. keep the times, route numbers, names, and quoted question as recorded. use plain language and connected paragraphs, not a table, and don't turn visual estimates into measurements.

finish with a short section identifying items for verification, including the usable door width, responsibility for moving deliveries, the south lift's status, the raised-looking tactile tile, the bus-stop kerb and van obstruction, and the help point's hearing loop and call logging. this should be a list of checks, not recommendations or assigned actions. do not add an owner, deadline, outcome, or claim that a problem was fixed. the station drawing in the field folder was marked “draft, rev. 2” and wasn't checked against the site; mention that limitation only if it helps explain why a location or dimension remains uncertain. there are no photographs in these notes, and no further inspection or passenger interviews were carried out after the listed visit. make the final paragraph about that boundary of the evidence, rather than repeating the opening or giving a general conclusion.", "output": "Prepare an accessibility audit briefing for Leonie, not Ellis, using the supplied field notes from the fictional 14 May visit to North Quay Interchange. The City Access Review Team conducted the visit; Mara Chen took notes and Tomas Reed checked the route. Cover the interchange and the adjoining Quay Street bus stops only, not the wider transit network. Give the facilities group a usable account of what was observed and what still needs checking, without issuing a pass/fail verdict. Clearly distinguish direct observations, staff explanations, and unresolved questions.

Use a short opening to state the date, team, and scope. Then organize the briefing in connected paragraphs under these numbered locations:

1. East entrance and lift lobby
2. Platform 2
3. Quay Street bus stops
4. Information and help point

At each location, keep observations distinct from attributed explanations and unknowns where applicable. Use plain language, not a table. Preserve the recorded times, route numbers, names, and quoted question. Do not turn visual estimates into measurements.

**1. East entrance and lift lobby**

The team began at the east entrance at 8:20 in light rain. The automatic doors opened on the first approach in three trials. The clear opening appeared narrower when a person stood beside the door, but no tape measurement was taken. The notes say the fixed sign may be reducing the usable width. Tactile paving leads from the entrance toward the lift lobby, but one strip ends about a metre short of the lobby threshold, leaving a smooth tile gap. At 8:34, a delivery trolley was parked partly over the strip; it was gone when the team returned at 9:05. Do not imply that it remained there all morning. The desk clerk said deliveries are usually moved before the peak, but the team did not ask who is responsible for moving them. A bench near the entrance has an armrest at only one end, and no reserved seating sign was seen.

The north lift was in service, while the south lift displayed an out-of-service notice with no return time. The nearest stairs are around the corner, rather than directly opposite the lobby. The north lift call button responded. A temporary event poster taped to the wall partly obscured the panel’s lower button row, but did not cover the buttons. The lift arrived after roughly 40 seconds on one observation; it was not timed on repeated trips. Its floor indicator worked, and the spoken floor announcement was audible from the doorway. The team did not assess its volume from the back of a crowded car. A staff member said the south lift had stopped that morning and that a contractor had been contacted. The review team did not have a work order, so present this as an attributed explanation, not a confirmed repair schedule.

**2. Platform 2**

The team followed the signed accessible route. At the corridor junction, a blue wayfinding arrow pointed toward platform 2 and the bus connection, but the smaller print below it was hard to read from the approach. The next sign was mounted behind a temporary queue barrier. A tactile warning surface was present at the platform entrance, though the edge of one tile looked raised. The team did not test it or estimate its height.

The platform-to-train interface varied by vehicle. On the train that arrived at 8:52, the gap looked wider near the second carriage than near the first. The train stopped with its first doorway just beyond the painted boarding marker. This was a visual observation from one arrival, not a measured gap or a statement about every train. No ramp was requested or deployed during the visit. A passenger asked the station host, “is the lift at the far end working today?” The host pointed back toward the lobby; the team could not hear the rest of their exchange.

**3. Quay Street bus stops**

The two bus stops are on opposite sides of the access road. The stop serving routes 6 and 18 has a shelter and a timetable case. The case was fogged inside, making the printed times unreadable during the visit. The stop for route 41 has a pole and no shelter. The kerb at the route 6/18 stop was not measured. At 9:18, a parked maintenance van partly blocked the landing area, although a gap remained open behind it. The driver was not present, and the team does not know how long the van stayed. The route 41 pole’s route label faced the road, while the small stop name plate faced the pavement. A route 6 driver lowered the vehicle ramp after a wheelchair user waited at the stop. Record only this one observed boarding: the team did not speak with the passenger or ask whether the ramp met their needs.

**4. Information and help point**

The departures screen in the main hall showed platform information for the next two trains. The team did not compare it with the live control system. The wall-mounted help point lit when pressed, and a voice answered after about 25 seconds. The team did not test the hearing loop or confirm whether the call was logged. The staff member who answered asked which entrance the caller was near, but the notes do not record the caller’s answer. Do not infer from the light and voice response that the help point is accessible in every respect. A printed large-text map was available at the information desk. The clerk said copies had run low; two were visible when the team checked at 9:40. No one asked for a copy during the visit.

**Items for verification**

End with a short list of checks, not recommendations or assigned actions. Include the usable door width; responsibility for moving deliveries; the south lift’s status; the raised-looking tactile tile; the bus-stop kerb and van obstruction; and the help point’s hearing loop and call logging. Do not add an owner, deadline, outcome, or claim that anything was fixed.

The station drawing in the field folder was marked “draft, rev. 2” and was not checked against the site. Mention that limitation only if it helps explain why a location or dimension remains uncertain. There are no photographs in these notes, and no further inspection or passenger interviews took place after the listed visit. Make the final paragraph about this boundary of the evidence, rather than repeating the opening or giving a general conclusion."}]
